title: Large language models discover complementary heuristics for combinatorial optimization - Nature Machine Intelligence
gist: Only the abstract is available (subscription preview): LACE, an LLM framework that structures algorithm design via an input/output schema, tool library and heuristic portfolio and evolves complementary specialist heuristics, scores 0.945 on 36 CO-Bench problems versus 0.870 for the best prior LLM method and 0.571 for direct prompting. On four new problems it hits 0.97-0.99 while five LLM baselines produce no feasible algorithm, suggesting gains come from scaffolding rather than the model.

insights.claim: Directly prompting LLMs to synthesize complete heuristics in a single pass routinely fails on new combinatorial optimization problems.
insights.speaker: Nature Machine Intelligence
insights.so_what: Value in applied AI for operations accrues to orchestration frameworks, not just foundation models.
insights.quote: single-pass synthesis of complete heuristics routinely fails on new CO problems

insights.claim: LACE decomposes algorithm design into an input schema, output schema, tool library and heuristic portfolio (the I-OTH interface), giving the LLM a verified problem contract so its capacity goes to high-level algorithmic reasoning rather than problem-specific implementation.
insights.speaker: Nature Machine Intelligence
insights.so_what: A reusable pattern for agentic code generation in enterprise optimization software.
insights.quote: directing model capacity to high-level algorithmic reasoning rather than problem-specific implementation

insights.claim: Across 36 classical CO-Bench problems, LACE averaged 0.945 versus 0.870 for the strongest existing LLM-based method and 0.571 for direct LLM prompting, which the authors say locates the gain in the framework rather than the model.
insights.speaker: Nature Machine Intelligence
insights.so_what: Framework design can nearly double performance versus naive prompting with the same model.
insights.quote: LACE attains an average score of 0.945, against 0.870 for the strongest existing LLM-based method and 0.571 for direct LLM prompting without any framework

insights.claim: Designing effective heuristics for each new combinatorial optimization variant in manufacturing, logistics, healthcare operations and energy management traditionally requires deep domain knowledge and months of expert iteration.
insights.speaker: Nature Machine Intelligence
insights.so_what: Automation could compress operations-research consulting and solver-customization costs.
insights.quote: designing effective heuristics for each new problem variant requires deep domain knowledge and months of expert iteration

insights.claim: On four structurally new combinatorial problems, LACE scored 0.97-0.99 while five existing LLM-based baselines failed to produce any feasible algorithm.
insights.speaker: Nature Machine Intelligence
insights.so_what: Zero-shot generalization to novel problems is where structured agents decisively separate from competitors.
insights.quote: On four structurally new problems, LACE reaches 0.97–0.99, while five existing LLM-based baselines fail to produce any feasible algorithm.

insights.claim: Complementary evolution iteratively generates and selects specialist heuristics that together solve heterogeneous instances within strict runtime budgets, and the authors conclude algorithm discovery for such problems can be automated to a substantial degree.
insights.speaker: Nature Machine Intelligence
insights.so_what: Portfolio-of-specialists approach suits production settings with diverse instances and latency limits.
insights.quote: effective algorithm discovery for such problems can be automated to a substantial degree

insights.claim: LACE is reported as robust across frontier LLM backbones with varying cost-efficiency trade-offs, and its code is released openly under the MIT licence.
insights.speaker: Nature Machine Intelligence
insights.so_what: Model-agnostic, open-source tooling lowers vendor lock-in and commoditizes the capability.
insights.quote: LACE is robust across frontier LLM backbones with varying cost-efficiency trade-offs.
